the Med diet plus olive oil reduces the risk of diabetes more than a low-fat diet, but the Med diet plus nuts does not.

in patients at high cardiovascular risk, the Mediterranean diet plus olive or nuts reduced the risk for diabetes by approximately 40% compared to a low-fat diet, but the Mediterranean diet plus nuts did not have a statistically significant effect.

in patients at high cardiovascular risk, a Mediterranean-style diet with extra-virgin oil (EVO) reduced the risk for developing diabetes by 40%, whereas a Mediterranean diet with nuts reduced the risk for diabetes by only 17% compared with a low-fat diet at a median 4 years of follow-up.
